_readme: Sourced model guide. Every entry needs a source URL and a verified date. confidence: official (vendor docs / the CLI's own catalog), third-party (blog/benchmark site, treat as a hint), unknown (no source found; do NOT fill in from memory). `delegate check` compares this file with each CLI's live model list and flags new, removed and stale items. Local refreshes go to ~/.cli-delegate/model-guide.local.json and override entries with the same `key`.

sources.codex_live: codex debug models (the CLI's own catalog)

best_for: when opus at higher effort still falls short
entries.notes: Slower; $10/$50 per MTok; default effort high; retirement not sooner than 2027-09-01.

best_for: Anthropic's stated default starting point for most workloads
entries.notes: Moderate latency; $4/$20 per MTok; default effort medium; retirement not sooner than 2027-09-22.

best_for: best combination of speed and intelligence
entries.notes: Fast; $2/$10 per MTok; default effort high; retirement not sooner than 2027-09-28.
Fastest; $1/$5 per MTok; API docs list effort as not supported (the CLI still accepted --effort in tests); retirement not sooner than 2026-10-15, so check before relying on it.

best_for: a Claude-family second opinion using Agy's quota instead of Claude Code's
entries.notes: Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 are listed by Anthropic as legacy (still available). No strengths beyond that were found.

best_for: easier tasks where speed and cost matter
entries.notes: OpenAI: most efficient model for focused, high-volume tasks. Codex catalog: fast and affordable for easier tasks. A third-party comparison (gradually.ai, benchlm.ai) reports GPT-5.6 Terra ahead of GPT-6 Luna on a public coding lane (64.2 vs 51.1), so do not use Luna for hard coding.
Codex catalog calls it an older balanced model for straightforward work. Third-party sources put it as GPT-5.5-class at half the price.
Codex catalog: older fast and efficient model.
Codex catalog: legacy coding model. Supports efforts up to xhigh only.
Google: most intelligent Flash model, stable. Google's model card reports DeepSWE v1.1 73.7% vs 65.3% for 3.7 Flash (vendor figures). -low/-medium/-high in the id is the effort tier.
Google: previous-generation Flash, stable. Prefer 3.8 unless you need a different cost or behavior.
Google: previous-generation Flash balancing speed and multimodal capability, stable.
Google lists it as Preview: behavior and availability can change or be shut down (Gemini 3 Pro Preview already was), so re-run `delegate check` before depending on it.

Model card: 117B total / 5.1B active params, Apache 2.0, reasoning levels low/medium/high. Coding strength is NOT stated in the model card, so do not assume it is good at code: check `delegate scoreboard` for your own results first.

OpenAI: built for the hardest end-to-end work. $10 in / $50 out per MTok, 1.05M context. Codex catalog: frontier intelligence for the most demanding work; its default effort is low, so always pass --effort. Most expensive Codex option: reserve for jobs a cheaper model failed.

OpenAI: built for complex coding and agentic workflows. $2 in / $10 out per MTok, 1.05M context. Codex catalog: workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Sensible default worker for real implementation jobs.
Codex catalog: older coding model for complex work. Prefer gpt-6-sol unless you need to compare.
